transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-11
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Moretti (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Aureline VP Eng), Tom Wallace (Aureline SRE), Angela Moreno (Aureline ML)

Summary: quick sync on last week's microburst tests, TTFT regressions on streaming path, and kernel selection tradeoffs. Actioned a 1k-sample microburst run and to exchange kernel traces + config. Some noise on transcription around KV cache and quant names (seen as "KV cash" or "quant-2x") so please treat names in traces as primary.

Topics: TTFT spikes, streaming handshake delay, sequence length distribution, kernel selection (matmul vs fused attention), prefix/KV caching behavior, fallback/hedging strategies.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, short agenda today — 30 to 45 minutes. main things: review the microburst numbers you sent, go over the handshake/streaming first-token variance, and pick a kernel set to continue the pilot with.
00:22 Priya (Aureline): thanks Maya. we got your notes. Tom is gonna walk through the numbers first.
00:30 Tom (Aureline): yeah, so we ran the weekend stress with the sim harness. quick note: our seqlen distribution is kinda long tail — median 48 tokens but 95th at 290 and occasional 1k sequences. attached charts are in the drive. the microbursts we saw have p50 at 60ms, p95 at 420ms, p99 spikes to 1.2s. most of the p99 tied to first-token where dense seqs coincide with cold caches.
01:05 Luca (Redwood): okay that fits the pattern of TTFT being dominated by kernel selection and the KV warmup for streaming. did you run with prefix caching enabled on the staging cluster?
01:12 Tom: we left prefix caching off to mirror prod right now, that's why some of the cold-starts look worse.
01:18 Maya: right, and that was by design, but for the pilot we need a 48hr run with prefix enabled to understand steady-state. Luca, can you enable a staging KV prefix cache?
01:25 Luca: yep, I'll flip it on for the next 48 hours after this call and share the config. note: our prefix caching heuristics are adaptive — they'll cache at the route level if sequence id entropy is low. if you have many unique session ids, cache hit-rate drops.
01:44 Priya: our sessions are fairly sticky for chat flows, but we do have occasional high-cardinality ingestion for API-batches from partners.
01:52 Angela: quick Q — on the kernels, your last trial used fused-attn-16b then backfilled with matmul-compat for long seqs, correct? I think the sheet said fused was faster for short seqs but blew up at 512+.
02:08 Luca: yup, that's it. fused-attn (fastpath) wins for <=256 typically but beyond that the matmul/FFT-like kernel is more stable memory-wise. for the 1k sequences we've been hedging with dynamic kernel swap.
02:22 Tom: we saw the swap work but there's a 30–60ms penalty on the swap itself that affects TTFT for streaming clients.
02:30 Maya: can you clarify — is the swap synchronous on the request path or prepped during prefix?
02:36 Luca: currently synchronous the first time a sequence hits that path. we can pre-warm by running a background kernel init for likely seqlen buckets (warm threads), but that costs GPU mem and startup time on the node.
02:48 Priya: what's the practical trade? more memory for fewer TTFT spikes?
02:52 Luca: yes. pre-warm reduces first-token variance at the cost of reserved memory and a small steady-state overhead. another lever is microbatch hedging — we keep a small pool of primed workers for long-seq requests. that helps microburst head-of-line blocking.
03:10 Angela: also wondering about quant. we tested int8 static quant and saw a slight drop in tail latency but some output quality jitter on our eval prompts. is Redwood recommending hybrid quant for this pilot?
03:24 Maya: for pilots we usually recommend quant profiles that are validated on your eval set — Redwood Optimize has a prescriptive profile generator. if quality is sensitive at p99 we lean towards fp16 for the headpath and int8/qat on the background fallback variants.
03:40 Tom: any concerns about KMS or key rotation when enabling caching and longer-lived sessions? security flagged rotation windows as a potential issue.
03:48 Maya: noted — our Private stack supports customer-managed KMS and the cache keys don't persist outside the node in plaintext. we'll send the security note — but Luca, let's include the caching lifecycle in the security packet.
03:59 Luca: will do.
04:05 Priya: ok back to microbursts — the dataset we sent had synthetic partner bursts — which maybe aren't identical to prod. Angela, can you run the 1k scripted microburst with the real session id distribution?
04:18 Angela: yeah I can, I need to adapt the harness. I'll run it and put results in the shared drive.
04:23 Maya: perfect. timeline on that?
04:25 Angela: aiming to have results by Friday (2027-01-15).
04:29 Maya: great.
04:32 [05:00] (brief cross talk; background noise)
05:25 Tom: small note — when we ran RunFastAI last quarter their hedging model lowered p99 but increased p50 slightly. curious if Redwood's hedging will behave similarly.
05:35 Luca: yeah hedging trades some steady-state cost for tail reductions. our hedging supports async reroute and speculative execution for the earliest tokens which helps streaming TTFT if the speculative pipeline is primed.
05:48 Priya: speculative exec sounds expensive — do we have ballpark cost changes?
05:53 Maya: depends on traffic shape. for our estimates we provided a per-token delta and an amortized hedging overhead. we'll push a modeled cost table to the sheet.
06:05 Tom: can you also annotate the kernel traces with cuda kernel names? our perf team prefers that for root-cause. we got obfuscated names from last run.
06:12 Luca: yes, I'll include symbolized kernel traces and map them to the fused vs matmul buckets. note sometimes the vendor driver shows vendor-specific names that get munged, but we'll include raw timestamps.
06:24 Angela: FYI there's a subtle mismatch: our prod scheduler has short preemption windows that occasionally tear down warm workers. could that explain intermittent cold starts?
06:34 Luca: absolutely, if the node preempts primed workers the prefix cache effectiveness drops and you'll see TTFT jitter. one mitigation: pin a small reserved pool for the Redwood Dedicated workers or set higher eviction thresholds on nodes.
06:48 Priya: we're evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput, but the folks in procurement want numbers. can we produce a small RIO (rough order) of cost vs TTFT improvement?
06:58 Maya: yes — action item to produce a cost/SLO table comparing hosted with hedging vs dedicated with pre-warmed pools. I'll own that.
07:07 Priya: thanks.
07:10 [12:10] (transcription hiccup: "KV cash" appears in some lines; meaning KV cache)
07:35 Tom: one specific oddity — when we switched kernels mid-stream one request hit an OOM on the HW and retried on fallback which caused duplication and another delay. should we set an upper cap on sequence size to force fallback earlier?
07:50 Luca: we can enforce sequence size cutoff at the routing layer and direct >512 into a long-seq pool. that avoids unexpected OOMs on fastpath kernels. downside: you lose latency for sequences that are actually short but falsely tagged, but we can use a per-request hint header to route accurately.
08:12 Angela: we can add hint headers on the client side (session metadata). I'll work with the API team.
08:18 Maya: good.
08:20 Priya: just to be explicit — the success criteria for this week: reduce TTFT p99 from 1.2s to under 600ms in staging with prefix caching on and without quality regressions >1% on our eval set. is that fair?
08:36 Maya: yes that sounds reasonable as a pilot milestone. Luca — do you think that's achievable with pre-warm + kernel choices?
08:42 Luca: achievable with the hedging + pre-warm plan and sequence cutoff. quant may complicate quality, so plan is fp16 head, int8 fallback, pre-warm long-seq kernels, enable prefix for 48h, run 1k microburst workload.
09:00 Tom: one more data ask: can you give per-kernel invocation latency distribution? we want to correlate high-latency kernels to node/driver cycles.
09:10 Luca: yes, will attach per-kernel histograms and a per-node breakdown.
09:16 Maya: ok let's walk through the concrete next steps and owners.
09:20 Priya: before that, any blockers on security? procurement mentioned SOC2 scope and audit logs availability for Dedicated.
09:28 Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we will attach the attestation and point to our audit log retention options. Luca — can you drop the compliance pack link?
09:35 Luca: link to compliance pack will be shared in the follow-up email.
09:40 Maya: perfect.
09:42 Recap / Action Items:
- Maya: share kernel-selection spreadsheet with annotated traces + cost/SLO table — due 2027-01-13
- Luca: enable prefix KV cache on staging pilot for 48h and attach the config + per-kernel histograms — due 2027-01-14
- Angela: run 1k microburst with real session-id distro and upload results — due 2027-01-15
- Tom: provide 24h seqlen histogram and p50/p95/p99 latency from prod — due 2027-01-13
- Priya: confirm procurement windows for Dedicated ROI — tentative by 2027-01-20

Closing notes: decided to trial pre-warming for long-seq kernels + prefix caching for the next 48h. main risk areas: memory reservation for pre-warm, quality impact from quant, and scheduler preemption in prod. next sync: propose 2027-01-18 for a 60-minute deep perf session (Maya to propose times).

End of call.
